title: Lo, How a Rose E'er Blooming
description: Lo, How a Rose E'er Blooming in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Fridrich Layriz, first published in 1500. The English translation is by Theodore Baker and Harriet Reynolds Krauth and Harriet Reynolds Spaeth and John Casper Mattes (1894). The tune, ES IST EIN ROS ENTSPRUNGEN (RHYTHMIC), is from Altes Catholische Geistliche Kirchengeseng, Köln, 1599. This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Lo, how a Rose e'er bloom-ing from ten-der stem hath sprung! Of Jes-se's lin-eage com-ing, as men of old have sung. It came, a flow'r-et bright, a-mid the cold of win-ter, When half spent was the night.

lines: Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming
as men of old have sung.
When half spent was the night.
the Rose I have in mind;
she bore to men a Savior,
When half spent was the night.
How Christ, the Lord of glory
was born on earth this night.
and in the manger found Him,
from sin and death He saves us,
Bring us at length we pray,
to the bright courts of Heaven,

reviewNotes: Held back: the score has no time signature (a chant or free rhythm), which the solfa grid cannot bar; bar 3 has 6 beats, more than 4; bar 4 has 6 beats, more than 4; bar 5 has 5 beats, more than 4; bar 7 has 6 beats, more than 4; bar 8 has 6 beats, more than 4; bar 13 has 6 beats, more than 4; bar 14 has 6 beats, more than 4.
